A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ISAC research, with matching authors, core framework and retained experiments. Their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial revision.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-generation experiments, baseline comparisons, ablations and qualitative analyses in Section 5 and the appendices, including Tables 1–4 and 8–11.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds compositional benchmarks, layout-conditioned generation, latent-selection results, quality analyses and seed-variability measurements in Section 4 and the appendices.

M1.justification: v1 combines instance separation with a class-overlap penalty. v2 Section 3.3 extends this to explicit token-pair repulsion and attribute binding, introducing a binding loss absent from v1. Appendix C.1 also adds an alternative inference procedure that selects candidates using accumulated ISAC losses without backpropagation. The underlying clustering, MPO and attention-propagation components remain.

E1.justification: v2 adds HRS-Bench evaluations, color/texture/complex-composition tasks from T2I-CompBench, and layout-conditioned generation with overlapping boxes. These extend v1's counting-focused coverage substantially. IntraCompBench retains the earlier COCO-derived benchmark's classes and prompt construction; its new name does not establish new coverage. T2I-CompBench Numeracy also already appeared in v1 as T2I-CompBench++ Numeracy.

E2.justification: v2 adds Self-Cross to SD1.5 and SD3.5-M comparisons and evaluates A&E, SynGen, InitNO and TEBOpt against ISAC on SD3.5-M, where v1 lacked those comparisons. CountGen is newly evaluated on SDXL, while GLIGEN and CAR&SAR support the new layout comparison. Bounded Attention receives qualitative comparisons. Counting Guidance and the TokenCompose/IterComp comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: New protocols include reuse of released HRS-Bench box layouts, best-of-10 selection on Flux.1-dev and Qwen-Image, and FID/CMMD measurements against native SDXL outputs. Original COCO sampling and detector-ensemble procedures remain. However, v2 Section 4.1 describes exact-count/all-class success while Appendix A.2 retains fractional detection accuracy, leaving any actual change to that scoring procedure unresolved.

E4.justification: v2 adds a semantic-overlap heatmap, CountGen-combination analysis, distributional image-quality evaluation, attention-layer ablation and a transparent-object failure case (Figure 2, Tables 10/13/14 and Figure 15). Earlier schedule, MPO and clustering ablations remain. Conversely, v1's separate propagation/normalization diagnostics and SDXL-Turbo dynamics analysis are removed, rather than merely relocated.

E5.justification: v1 reports multiple images and qualitative seed examples but provides no uncertainty estimates for its Numeracy table. v2 Appendix C.4 and Table 16 newly report 30 seeds and means with standard deviations for SD1.5/SDXL Numeracy results. This reporting improvement is confined to that evaluation; v1's unspecified Numeracy run count prevents inferring an explicit increase in runs.

E6.justification: Many original COCO scores and ablation values persist, but v2 adds substantial compositional, layout, comparator and latent-selection results. For example, its new layout experiment reports GLIGEN counting F1 of 66.58 without ISAC and 71.28 with ISAC. Numeracy values change from 54.3% to 55.0% for SD1.5+ISAC, 50.7% to 51.1% for SDXL, and 63.4% to 64.0% for SDXL+ISAC, now with 30-seed reporting; these are not established same-setting gains. Changed SD1.5 efficiency values in v2 Table 2 remain unreconciled with the older values retained in Table 15.

T1.justification: v2 formally defines repulsion/binding token-pair sets and the binding objective based on 1 minus MPO in Section 3.3, extending v1's class-only objective. The central MPO, foreground-mask, clustering and attention-propagation definitions remain mathematically equivalent. Neither version supplies theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The instance-first thesis remains, but v2 broadens the central contribution to attribute binding and both text-to-image and layout-to-image control. Its abstract, introduction and conclusion foreground three-benchmark validation, superiority over count-supervised approaches and IntraCompBench as a named contribution. v1 principally emphasized improved class/instance generation and the reported 52%/83% accuracies.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive interpretations of CountGen's mask proposals, failures of exclusive box masking, image-quality tradeoffs and seed stability. It also identifies ambiguous parsed counts and missing 3D understanding as applicability limits. The runtime limitation remains, while v1's argument that normalization prevents transferring several baselines and its proposed SDXL-Turbo extension are removed.

D1.justification: v2 documents GPT-OSS-20B prompt parsing through instructions, examples and approximate cost, specifies normalized coordinates and bilinear attention upsampling, and identifies the reused layout annotations. This substantially expands implementation information beyond v1's assumed class/count inputs. However, v1's blanket single-A100-80GB experimental hardware statement is no longer provided. Both versions still promise code upon publication.

R1.justification: Related work is substantially reframed around training-free guidance, count supervision, layout control and benchmark limitations. New discussions include Self-Cross, GLIGEN, Attention Refocusing, HRS-Bench, OverLayBench and TIFA. CountGen, already cited in v1 as Make It Count, receives substantive comparative and complementarity analysis. The earlier MCR/TweedieMix discussion and several segmentation/distillation references disappear.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work and method exposition are extensively rewritten. Separate preliminaries are condensed into method background, the method is organized into named phases and a scheduling subsection, and experiments and appendices are substantially reorganized. Terminology changes from class disambiguation to semantic separation accompany this broader narrative revision.

P2.justification: v2 replaces the opening comparison, redraws the method overview, restructures the main results table and adds heatmaps, parser examples, layout comparisons, failure illustrations and analysis tables. Several earlier standalone figures disappear. Retained displays are distinguishable from additions: for example, v1 Figure 2 becomes v2 Figure 3, and v1 Figure 15 becomes v2 Figure 22.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens validation beyond v1's largely counting-focused evidence: Tables 2–4 add broader compositional tasks, comparisons on SD3.5-M and layout evaluation using shared box inputs. Parser documentation, quantified seed variability and concrete failure analyses address important reproducibility and applicability gaps. Conflicting exact-versus-fractional accuracy definitions and unreconciled efficiency figures weaken reporting, and the quality metrics measure deviation from SDXL rather than directly proving aesthetic preservation. Nevertheless, the expanded comparative evidence and methodological documentation provide a substantial net improvement.
